title: A collection that changes
bodyMd:
A botanical garden stores seeds in a cool, dry room. The collection is not simply left untouched: staff periodically test a small sample from each batch for germination. If too few seeds germinate, they grow plants from the remaining viable seeds and collect a fresh generation. This renewal prevents a batch from becoming useless merely because its seeds have aged.

Renewal nevertheless presents a difficulty. If only a few parent plants contribute to the replacement batch, the new seeds may represent less of the original population's genetic variation. Staff therefore record both germination rates and the number of parent plants used. A high germination rate describes the condition of the stored seeds, but by itself it does not establish that the collection still represents the population from which it came.
